BackstoryDef.title: Trident farmhand
BackstoryDef.description: Raised beside fertile rivers, they learned planting, harvesting, and how quickly a flooded field could erase a season's work.

BackstoryDef.title: Village smith's apprentice
BackstoryDef.description: Their master repaired plows, horseshoes, axes, and weapons for travelers moving along the river roads.

BackstoryDef.title: Ford builder's child
BackstoryDef.description: They helped maintain bridges, ferries, embankments, and roads constantly threatened by spring floods.

BackstoryDef.title: Riverside singer
BackstoryDef.description: They earned meals by carrying songs and stories between inns, villages, and the countless crossings of the Riverlands.

BackstoryDef.title: River lord's ward
BackstoryDef.description: Fostered in another lord's hall, they learned how quickly friendship and rivalry could change along the Trident.

BackstoryDef.title: Heir of the Crossing Fields
BackstoryDef.description: Their childhood lessons covered tenants, harvests, river tolls, and the complicated loyalties of neighboring Houses.

BackstoryDef.title: Second son of the Trident
BackstoryDef.description: With the estate promised to an elder sibling, they spent their days riding, hunting, and practicing for service under another lord.

BackstoryDef.title: Rivers bastard
BackstoryDef.description: Known by the bastard name Rivers, they learned to find a place among commoners and nobles without fully belonging to either.

BackstoryDef.title: Marsh hunter
BackstoryDef.description: They hunted waterfowl and small game among reeds, muddy banks, and mist-covered streams.

BackstoryDef.title: Riverrun page
BackstoryDef.description: They carried messages, tended horses, and watched knights drill in the yards of a river lord.

BackstoryDef.title: Trident farmer
BackstoryDef.description: Rich soil made farming productive, though war and flooding taught them never to trust a peaceful season.

BackstoryDef.title: Crossroads smith
BackstoryDef.description: Travelers, merchants, farmers, and soldiers all brought damaged tools and weapons to their roadside forge.

BackstoryDef.title: River mason
BackstoryDef.description: They built bridges, mills, dikes, and stone foundations capable of surviving high water.

BackstoryDef.title: Reedland hunter
BackstoryDef.description: They could track game through mud and reeds while moving quietly enough to avoid both prey and unwanted soldiers.

BackstoryDef.title: Traveling minstrel
BackstoryDef.description: Inns and noble halls along the river roads kept them fed so long as their songs were entertaining.

BackstoryDef.title: Village midwife
BackstoryDef.description: They delivered children, treated fever, and knew which herbs grew best along wet riverbanks.

BackstoryDef.title: Septon's clerk
BackstoryDef.description: Their education came from copying records, reading letters, and settling humble disputes for villagers unable to write.

BackstoryDef.title: Riverland man-at-arms
BackstoryDef.description: They have marched beneath more than one banner, as Riverland loyalties have a habit of shifting whenever great lords quarrel.

BackstoryDef.title: Estate reeve
BackstoryDef.description: They collected rents, measured harvests, and settled arguments among tenants for a local House.

BackstoryDef.title: Trident negotiator
BackstoryDef.description: They became skilled at settling grazing rights, toll disputes, and old feuds before swords were drawn.
